name: Eliab (Eliab, son of Helon, leader from the tribe of Zebulun)
title: Leader of the Tribe of Zebulun
summary: Eliab, son of Helon, was the chosen leader and chief of the tribe of Zebulun during the wilderness journey. He was appointed by God to assist Moses in the census at the desert of Sinai and represented his tribe at the dedication of the tabernacle. He played an important administrative and military role in organizing the people of Israel during their exodus from Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as Leader of Zebulun
keyEvents.description: God appointed Eliab, son of Helon, as leader of the tribe of Zebulun to assist Moses and Aaron in the census.

keyEvents.title: The Census at Sinai
keyEvents.description: Eliab led the counting of the tribe of Zebulun, which numbered 57,400 men fit for war over twenty years old.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement Around the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: The tribe of Zebulun, under Eliab's leadership, was placed on the east side of the tabernacle, together with Judah and Issachar, under the banner of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Offering at the Dedication of the Altar
keyEvents.description: Eliab presented his offering on the third day during the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle, including a silver plate, a silver basin, a gold bowl, as well as burnt and sin offerings.

keyEvents.title: Departure from Sinai
keyEvents.description: When the people of Israel broke camp from the wilderness of Sinai, the division of Zebulun under Eliab's leadership marched as part of the camp of Judah.
